questions.text: An ammeter has an upper measurement limit of $200$ mA. What shunt resistance must be used to measure currents up to $1000$ mA with it ($\Omega$)? The resistance of the ammeter is $12~\Omega$.
The resistance of a shunt connected in parallel with an ammeter is $5$ times smaller than the resistance of the ammeter. If the ammeter reads $100$ mA, what is the current $I$ in the main line (mA)?
The resistance of the shunt is $R$ and the resistance of the ammeter is $4R$. If the current in the main line is $I=600$ mA, what current does the ammeter read (mA)?
What must the resistance of a shunt connected to an ammeter with an internal resistance of $180~\Omega$ be in order to increase its measurement range $9$ times ($\Omega$)?

The internal resistance of an ammeter is $12~\Omega$ and it is designed to measure currents up to $2.5$ A. To measure currents up to $15$ A with this ammeter, what shunt (in $\Omega$) must be connected to it?

The internal resistance of an ammeter connected in a circuit is $11~\Omega$ and the resistance of the shunt is $2.2~\Omega$. If the ammeter reads a current of $13$ A, what is the current in the circuit (in amperes)?

If one of two identical shunts is connected to an ammeter, its scale division value increases $3$ times. By what factor does the measurement range of the ammeter increase if both shunts are connected to it in parallel?

Two identical shunts are connected to each other in series and then to an ammeter; its measurement range increases $4.5$ times. By what factor does the measurement range of the ammeter increase if both shunts are connected to it in parallel?

An ammeter of resistance $0.04~\Omega$ has a copper wire $15$ cm long with a cross-sectional area of $3$ mm$^2$ connected in parallel with it. The ammeter reads a current of $0.17$ A. Find the current in the wire (A). The resistivity of copper is $1.7\cdot10^{-8}~\Omega\cdot$m.
The internal resistance of a voltmeter is $300~\Omega$. By what factor does the scale division value change if a series (multiplier) resistance of $1200~\Omega$ is connected to it?

The internal resistance of a voltmeter is $2$ k$\Omega$ and it is designed to measure $8$ V. What series (multiplier) resistance (k$\Omega$) must be connected to this voltmeter so that it can measure a voltage of $40$ V?

A voltmeter of resistance $1600~\Omega$ is designed to measure voltages up to $15$ V. What series (multiplier) resistance must be connected to it so that this voltmeter can measure voltages up to $210$ V ($\Omega$)?
What resistance must be connected to a voltmeter designed to measure $15$ V so that it can measure a voltage of $270$ V ($\Omega$)? The resistance of the voltmeter is $300~\Omega$.
A voltmeter is designed to measure $20$ V. To measure a voltage of $150$ V with it, what series (multiplier) resistance ($\Omega$) must be connected to it? $R_v=200~\Omega$.
A voltmeter with an internal resistance of $2800~\Omega$, connected to the mains, reads $120$ V. What resistance (in $\Omega$) must be connected in series with the voltmeter so that it reads $80$ V?
In the circuit, $R_1=800~\Omega$, $R_2=1000~\Omega$, and the total resistance of this circuit is $480~\Omega$. By what factor has the measurement range of the voltmeter been increased?
